_handoff: Two sources are stitched at this date. ISC's reviewed Bulletin carries the
JMA catalogue (complete to about M2 around Japan) but lags ~20 months, so
it covers everything BEFORE the handoff. USGS ComCat is current to
yesterday but holds nothing below M3 in this region, so it covers the tail.
Refresh the boundary with:  python scripts/fetch_quakes.py --detect-handoff

isc.name: ISC Bulletin (includes JMA)
_max_events_per_request: ISC hard-caps a response at 55000 events and answers HTTP 413 above
that. Staying under the cap means the splitter is driven by our own
row count instead of a wasted round trip that gets rejected.
